title: Synthetic cutover validation with transactional rollback checks and staged load-shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a synthetic active->passive cutover validation that verifies backup/restore integrity at transaction boundaries, exercises circuit breaker thresholds, and validates staged load-shedding heuristics. This ticket defines the runbook, verification checks, observability assertions, and communication play for a non-customer-facing drill that simulates partial region degradation and a controlled promotion of the passive region. The drill must include end-to-end transaction-level checksum validation, KV and prefix cache reconciliation, time-skew detection, and automated rollback verification for in-flight requests.
acceptance_criteria: A runbook exists and is reviewed by SRE, Platform, and Product owners
Automated synthetic traffic generator can drive 3 classes of workload: short-chat, long-context, and embeddings
Backup restore validation completes with byte-level checksum match for primary tokenstore and metadata DB
Circuit breaker thresholds are validated: slow-path trigger at 200ms p95 and open when error-rate > 5% over 30s
Staged load-shedding policy drops low-priority background requests first and maintains P95 latency SLO for priority routes
Rollback verification is automatic: reconfiguration back to primary is exercised and traced with correlation IDs
All observability assertions (span counts, error budget burn rates, tracing continuity) pass in the verification dashboard
steps: Pre-drill: announce window to stakeholders and mark test region; snapshot runbook in Confluence
Pre-drill: run full backups of tokenstore and metadata DB and push manifests to S3 with immutable tags
Pre-drill: verify cross-region clock skew < 2s and rotate checkpoint TTLs for the experiment
Phase 1 - Canary: route 1% synthetic traffic to passive region using smart routing policy; compare latencies and success rate
Phase 2 - Incremental promotion: increase to 25% traffic slice and enable KV cache warming on passive; run transactional checksum validation on sampled writes
Phase 3 - Full promotion: switch control-plane routing to passive for tested tenant slice; run full backup-restore validation and end-to-end test suite
Exercise circuit breaker: inject latency on primary downstream to verify open/close behavior and fallback to passive model variants
Invoke staged load-shedding: ramp synthetic background load and confirm low-priority routes are shed while high-priority SLOs hold
Rollback rehearsal: trigger an automated rollback path with stepwise demotion and assert state convergence back to primary
Post-drill: collect artifacts, run reconciliation checks, and publish drill report
rollback_plan: Immediate: flip routing back to primary for control-plane and sync traffic to a canary subset
If KV divergence detected: halt writes on passive, snapshot current passive state, and run three-way merge probes between snapshots
If checksum mismatch persists: restore primary from pre-drill immutable snapshot and replay change-log to passive under validation harness
Escalation: paging list to include Platform lead, SRE on-call, and DB eng. Run manual audit of transactions using correlation IDs
Post-rollback: run end-to-end acceptance tests and keep primary as active for 2 maintenance cycles before reattempting drill
test_plan: Synthetic traffic scenarios: short-chat burst (50rps), long-context steady (8rps, windowed), heavy-embedding batch (2rps large-batch)
Failure injection: add 30-40% CPU noise on primary inference nodes and tail-latency delay on model serving path
Data integrity tests: byte-level checksum for tokenstore, row-count parity for metadata DB, and sample prompt->response deterministic hashes
Observability assertions: p95 latency, error-rate, span continuity, KV miss ratio, and cache warm-up curve
DR validation harness: automated acceptance scripts that fail the drill on any critical mismatch and capture forensic snapshots
notes: Prefer passive region with identical hardware profile to avoid performance skew
When sampling transactional checksums, use deterministic seed to ensure reproducibility
Coordinate with Controls team before touching KMS/HSM keys for snapshot access
Time-of-day matters: schedule outside high-cost billing windows to reduce impact on burst credits
